newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Bunds set for temporary decline to 102.49.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Bunds set for temporary decline to 102.49.

text.p: September Bund futures traded on LIFFE will pull back on Friday but longer term the bullish tone remains intact, technical analysts said.
"Bunds finally succumbed to the over bought conditions yesterday and corrected lower, breaking the accelerated uptrend," said David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.
"Subsequently we bounced up from 102.53 and the market is deciding whether it wants a deeper correction or whether to resume the powerful uptrend."
At 0659 GMT, September Bunds were at 102.87, up 0.16.
Sneddon said that while Bunds were below 102.94 to 102.90, considering the position of other debt markets, a deeper correction looked likely.
That area incorporated a price pivot area, an hourly high and the 61.8 percent retracement on the move down from July 9 high at 103.15.
"While below 102.94 it is short-term toppish and we would look for a move down to the 102.53, 49 band and likely lower to 102.30," he said.
"Essentially we are looking for a correction to unwind the extreme overbought condition in the market," said Sneddon.
If Bunds managed to get above 102.94, this would trigger a move back up to the recent high at 103.15, he said.
Robin Wilkin, senior technical analyst at MCM YieldWatch in London, saw a similar pattern for Bunds.
"A break of yesterday's low would confirm a setback to the 102.29, 102.09 support area, which is a 62 percent retracement of the 101.43-103.15 rally," he said.
A break down through there and a lower high for this session would confirm a short-term correction, he said.
Wilkin said below those supports a strong bull trendline came in at 102.18.
A break up through 103.15 would bring 103.30 into play and above there 103.50, he said.
At the short end, December Euromarks were unchanged at 96.75.
